question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The Yapese Empire, a maritime power in Micronesia's Caroline Islands that reached its peak around 1000 CE, is regarded as a thalassocracy--a political state whose dominance came from control of the sea rather than of territory. Scholars separate thalassocracies from tellurocracies, or land-based powers. ______ the British Empire (1600s-1900s CE) is famous for supremacy on both land and sea.
option a: In other words, empires are categorized according to the source of their power:
option b: Likewise, thalassocracies are powers based on the sea:
option c: Of course, the distinction is not always so tidy:
option d: For example, tellurocracies have long dominated their rivals:
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The British Empire's dual land-and-sea power shows the thalassocracy/tellurocracy split is not always clean, so a concession transition fits.

question: The student wants to present the study's research methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Suzanne K. Birner headed a study that analyzed seafloor rocks to shed light on the history of Earth's mantle. Samples were gathered from two ridges on the ocean floor. The team established when the samples formed (the Archean eon) and how oxidized they were (extremely low). The high temperatures of the Archean probably explain the rocks' low oxidation. Birner's group proposes that the mantle's oxidation has stayed constant over time, contradicting earlier theories. The results help account for the unusual conditions that made life on Earth possible.
option a: Birner headed a study aimed at understanding the history of Earth's mantle and explaining the conditions that allowed life to arise.
option b: Birner's team examined the age and oxidation levels of rock samples collected from two seafloor ridges.
option c: To probe the origins of Earth's unusual conditions further, the researchers concentrated on Archean-eon rocks, formed when Earth's temperatures were extremely high.
option d: By analyzing these ancient rocks, the team set out to challenge earlier theories about how Earth's mantle has changed over time.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice B describes what the researchers actually did--analyzing the age and oxidation of samples from two ridges--which is the research method.

question: The student wants to connect a quotation to a particular nontraditional design element in Cody's work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Melissa Cody is a Dine (Navajo) textile artist celebrated for merging traditional Dine motifs (stripes, zigzags, and diamond patterns) with nontraditional features. Her pieces incorporate arrangements of shapes or text drawn from video game graphics and pop culture. Cody: "I'm a child of '80s video game culture...I grew up with this world of pixelization." Cody: "The things we consider tradition now weren't considered tradition when they first came about." Her tapestry Dust presents blocky letters exposed through negative space over a contrasting diamond pattern. Her tapestry Walking Off No Water Mesa presents rectangular panes that reveal a stylized landscape patterned with contrasting colored diamonds.
option a: The blocky letters exposed through negative space in Dust echo Cody's childhood immersion in blocky video game graphics--what she calls "this world of pixelization."
option b: Cody's tapestry Dust includes a contrasting diamond pattern, a traditional design element that "we consider tradition now."
option c: Cody's upbringing as "a child of '80s video game culture" informed her choice to combine traditional and nontraditional design elements in Walking Off No Water Mesa.
option d: According to Cody, certain features of Walking Off No Water Mesa, such as the contrasting colored diamonds, "weren't considered tradition when they first came about."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A ties the pixelization quote directly to the blocky, video-game-style lettering in Dust, a nontraditional element.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Adult glass eels turn up off the coast of Maine, yet the eels start life in the Sargasso Sea, a biodiverse region of the North Atlantic where they are born and to which they later return to breed. Although biologists think they have pinpointed the general zone of the Sargasso Sea vital to the endangered eels' survival, how the animals spawn there remains largely unknown. Researchers believe that unraveling this mystery will improve conservation of glass eels and their habitat, which in turn would help sustain several other species that depend on the eels for food.
option a: It describes a role that glass eels and other species play in supporting the ecosystem of the Sargasso Sea.
option b: It indicates that the benefit of understanding how glass eels spawn reaches beyond the eels themselves.
option c: It suggests that scientists are more concerned about other species than about the glass eels' habitat.
option d: It presents a study finding that identifies the conditions required to ensure the survival of glass eels.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined clause shows that solving the spawning mystery benefits not just eels but other species that feed on them.

question: Based on the texts, the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely agree on which point? Text 1 For millennia, O'odham farmers in the Sonoran Desert of the southwestern US and northern Mexico have grown organ pipe fruit and beans, at times planting the two together so that the organ pipe cacti shade the tepary beans. This shading shields the tepary beans from the fiercest heat and light and helps keep soil moisture from evaporating. Text 2 Tepary beans tolerate desert conditions well but do best in shade. Taking a cue from O'odham farmers, who often deliberately plant tepary beans in the shade of sun-tolerant species such as organ pipe cacti to guard them from sun and heat, Gary Nabhan and colleagues grew tepary beans beneath solar panels in the Sonoran Desert; the plants thrived, leading Nabhan's group to conclude that the panels offer a benefit much like that of organ pipe cacti.
option a: Organ pipe cacti can supply shade that protects tepary beans from high-intensity heat and light.
option b: Compared with Nabhan's method, the O'odham approach has the benefit of yielding beans.
option c: Nabhan's team's technique could be adjusted to more actively prevent soil moisture from evaporating.
option d: Organ pipe cacti grow best in shaded spots, whereas tepary beans need no shade to flourish.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both texts state that organ pipe cacti shade tepary beans and protect them from harsh heat and light.

question: Which choice best describes how Aunt Polly is presented in the text? The following text is adapted from Mark Twain's 1876 novel The Adventures of Tom Sawyer. Aunt Polly is eating dinner with Tom, her mischievous young nephew. Aunt Polly put to [Tom] questions that were crafty and very deep, hoping to lure him into damaging admissions. Like many other simplehearted people, it was her pet vanity to imagine she possessed a gift for dark and mysterious diplomacy, and she delighted in viewing her most obvious ploys as marvels of sly cunning.
option a: The narrator emphasizes that Aunt Polly's intentions are good even when her behavior is rude.
option b: The narrator comically overstates Aunt Polly's view of herself as an intellectual.
option c: The narrator gently pokes fun at Aunt Polly's mistaken confidence in her own subtlety.
option d: The narrator portrays Aunt Polly as being excessively nosy about other people's private lives.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage lightly mocks Aunt Polly for believing her transparent schemes are clever, showing misplaced confidence in her subtlety.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the researcher's example? A graph titled "Days per Winter That Lakes Have Surface Ice" (y-axis: Days, from 0 to 200) presents data for three lakes--Oulujarvi, Mirror Lake, and Lake Neusiedl--across the winters of 1980-81 and 2005-06. Freshwater lakes at or above a latitude of 45 degrees north, such as Lake Mjosa in Norway, commonly build up surface ice in winter. A study spanning 1980 to 2006 found that, on the whole, the number of days per winter that such lakes carry measurable surface ice is falling. A researcher, however, argued that certain lakes have instead experienced a longer duration of ice, offering as an example ______
option a: both Mirror Lake and Oulujarvi, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than they did in the winter of 1980-81.
option b: both Lake Neusiedl and Oulujarvi, which had fewer than 195 days of ice in the winter of 1980-81.
option c: Lake Neusiedl, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than it did in the winter of 1980-81.
option d: both Lake Neusiedl and Oulujarvi, which had more than 105 days of ice in the winter of 2005-06.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only Lake Neusiedl shows an increase in ice days from 1980-81 to 2005-06, matching the researcher's claim of longer ice duration.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Although mammals as a group have the highest brain-to-body-size ratio of any vertebrates, a team led by paleontologist Ornella Bertrand shows that for the ten million years after the dinosaurs went extinct, that ratio actually declined in mammals: as they evolved to occupy newly opened ecological niches, their bodies grew faster than their brains. Competition for resources generally rewards intelligence and thus large, complex brains, yet during this stretch the plentiful resources relative to mammal population size probably eased competition and enabled body size to rise. Bertrand's team reasons that as populations grew, competition sharpened, producing conditions that ______
option a: heightened the advantage that large body size conferred on mammals in certain ecological niches.
option b: favored an evolutionary rise in brain size relative to body size among mammals.
option c: restricted resources so drastically that mammals struggled to secure enough food to maintain large brains.
option d: encouraged large-brained mammals to adapt to a range of ecological niches.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since competition favors intelligence and larger brains, intensifying competition would favor a rise in brain-to-body ratio, matching choice B.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? As juveniles, every white-necked jacobin hummingbird sports brilliant blue head feathers; upon reaching adulthood, males keep this blue plumage while most females molt into a dull green. Even so, 28% of adult female jacobins stay colored exactly like juveniles and adult males. Drawing on field observations in Panama, a research team reports that although adult males clearly prefer drab green adult females as mates, they also behave more aggressively toward those green females than toward blue-feathered adult females when competing for resources. The team therefore hypothesizes that ______
option a: coloration keeps green-feathered adult female jacobins from telling adult males apart from blue-feathered adult females.
option b: the share of blue-feathered females will grow until fewer than half of adult female jacobins are green-feathered.
option c: the blue head plumage of adult female jacobins is driven by one or more factors unrelated to attracting mates.
option d: adult male jacobins do not behave aggressively toward blue-headed juvenile jacobins when competing for resources.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because males prefer green females as mates yet blue females face less aggression over resources, the blue coloration likely persists for non-mating reasons.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Colonel Virgil Miller served in the United States 65th Infantry Regiment, a unit of the US Army based in Puerto Rico. In 2016, the United States Congress recognized Miller and the other members of the 65th Infantry Regiment with one of its highest ______ Congressional Gold Medal.
option a: honors the
option b: honors: the
option c: honors (the
option d: honors; the
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No additional punctuation is required between 'honors' and the phrase naming the medal.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Evelyn Waugh's celebrated 1945 novel about a college student who stays at his friend's country estate carries a title that many readers recognize instantly: Brideshead Revisited. Waugh's novel first bore a different ______ while writing and revising it, Waugh had intended to name the book A House of the Faith.
option a: title, though
option b: title, though;
option c: title, though,
option d: title; though
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon links the two independent clauses, with 'though' set off by a comma inside the first clause.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Even though its onboard laboratory let it analyze rock samples on-site, the 2011 Mars Curiosity rover could not store samples for later study. ______ in building the 2020 Mars Perseverance rover, structural analysis engineer Kevin Liu and other members of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory aimed to include a mechanism that could do precisely that.
option a: Hence,
option b: Earlier,
option c: Specifically,
option d: Similarly,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The team's goal follows as a consequence of Curiosity's limitation, so a cause-effect transition like 'Hence' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Yupno people of the remote Finisterre Range in Papua New Guinea do not measure age and possess no artificial devices (such as clocks) for tracking time, but this does not mean the Yupno are ______ time. As Rafael Nunez and colleagues have recently demonstrated, the Yupno language holds many temporal expressions, such as apma sonda, which translates to "last week."
option a: meticulous about
option b: preoccupied with
option c: inattentive to
option d: dependent on
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The many temporal expressions show the Yupno do pay attention to time, so 'inattentive to' is the sense the evidence contradicts.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "mastery" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Alice Dunbar Nelson's 1899 short story "The Fisherman of Pass Christian." Pass Christian is a city in the US state of Mississippi. On the beach at Pass Christian the swift breezes collide and clash, as if each were striving for the mastery of the air. The land-breeze comes down through the pines--resinous, fragrant, and cold--carrying breath-like memories of dim, dark woods shaded by countless pine-needles. The breeze off the Gulf is warm, soft, and languorous, drifting up from the south with its hint of tropical warmth.
option a: Skillfulness
option b: Familiarity
option c: Comprehension
option d: Domination
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The breezes collide and clash as each fights to rule the air, so 'mastery' means domination or control.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In the hunt for new impact craters on Mars, seismic monitoring and orbital imaging serve as data sources whose roles are ______: once vibrations picked up by seismic monitoring reveal roughly where an impact took place, researchers can examine orbital images of that fairly small stretch of rocky surface to pinpoint the new crater exactly.
option a: complementary
option b: redundant
option c: exhaustive
option d: interchangeable
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Each method supplies what the other lacks--rough location plus precise imaging--so their roles are complementary.

question: Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Vertical gene transfer refers to passing genetic material from a parent to its offspring; horizontal gene transfer, by contrast, refers to the exchange of genetic material between organisms that are not in a parent-offspring relationship. Although horizontal gene transfer occurs frequently among prokaryotes--single-celled organisms such as the bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis and Lactobacillus curvatus--it has seldom been observed among eukaryotes (multicellular organisms). New research, however, indicates that horizontal gene transfer happens more often in eukaryotes than was once believed.
option a: It argues that two biological phenomena are more alike than they may initially appear to be.
option b: It explains why a widespread perception of a biological process is mistaken.
option c: It points out a distinction between how two kinds of biological processes work.
option d: It contrasts the frequency with which a biological phenomenon has been detected in two categories of organisms.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined sentence contrasts the frequent occurrence of horizontal gene transfer in prokaryotes with its rarity in eukaryotes.

question: Based on the text, what would be the most reasonable next step for the students to take to accomplish their goal? In 2003, the US state of Ohio adopted rate stability regulations (RSRs), which limit how freely insurance companies can raise premiums (the recurring fees policyholders pay to keep their policies) after policies take effect. Though RSRs are meant to help consumers, Naoki Aizawa and Ami Ko observe that RSRs might cut insurers' profits enough that insurers leave the market, weakening the competitive pressure that usually holds down premiums on newly issued policies. To find out whether this happened in Ohio, the students first gather data on the number of insurers in the state for several years before and after 2003, along with the premiums for new policies those insurers offered.
option a: Compare changes over time in the insurer-count data the students gathered with changes over time in insurer-count data from another state that adopted RSRs but not during the same period
option b: Compare changes over time in the premium-price data the students gathered with changes over time in premiums for policies already in effect during the same period in an otherwise similar state that had not adopted RSRs
option c: Compare changes over time in each of the two kinds of data the students gathered with changes over time in the same kinds of data from Ohio for a period beginning several years after 2003
option d: Compare changes over time in each of the two kinds of data the students gathered with changes over time in comparable data for the same period from an otherwise similar state that had not adopted RSRs
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A valid comparison needs a similar state without RSRs over the same period as a control for both types of data, matching choice D.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Numerous studies have found a positive link between dissolved organic carbon and mercury levels in freshwater bodies untouched by human activity. But Enelton Fagnani, Jose Roberto Guimaraes, and Pedro Sergio Fadini failed to find this correlation when examining freshwater bodies disturbed by industrial activity, prompting some scientists to suggest the link might be specific to undisturbed waters. Yet Jeffrey D. Jeremiason and colleagues conducted a study of freshwater bodies disturbed by mining that produced results resembling those from studies of undisturbed waters, suggesting that ______
option a: disturbances tied to industrial activity affect significantly more freshwater bodies than disturbances tied to mining do.
option b: the effect of industrial activity on the link between dissolved organic carbon and mercury levels should not be treated as representative of the effect of every kind of human disturbance.
option c: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in freshwater bodies disturbed by industrial activity than in those disturbed by mining.
option d: Fagnani, Guimaraes, and Fadini's study measured mercury concentration in fresh water using different methods than Jeremiason and colleagues' study did.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because mining-disturbed waters showed the correlation like undisturbed ones, the industrial result cannot stand for all human disturbances.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Astronomers Annie and Edward Maunder carefully examined historical records of the dark patches on the sun's surface called sunspots. Their late-1800s research led to identifying a span from 1645 to 1715--now called the Maunder ______ sunspots were remarkably scarce, a phenomenon that solar physicists continue to investigate.
option a: Minimum when
option b: Minimum, when
option c: Minimum: when
option d: Minimum--when
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma sets off the nonrestrictive 'when' clause describing the Maunder Minimum.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? When ranking the branches of the Kvichak River system, cartographers usually start at the system's lowest point, the Kvichak River. ______ hydrologists start at the top of the system, with the American River and the other tributaries fed by the system's source, the Alaska Range.
option a: In a similar way,
option b: For example,
option c: By contrast,
option d: In other words,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Cartographers start at the bottom while hydrologists start at the top, an opposition signaled by 'By contrast.'
